rooms.105800: The Kalveh Gatehouse squats astride the gravel road, a low tower of grey fieldstone with its portcullis cranked up and its timber gates standing open. Moss furs the lower courses, and a baron's banner, faded to the colour of old wine, hangs limp from a pole above the arch. The way north passes under the vault toward the edge of the great forest, while the gravel road runs on south into the baron's lands. Wheel ruts and hoofprints churn the mud under the arch.
rooms.105801: Gravel crunches underfoot on a road laid straight and kept in good repair, ditched on either side and edged with rough stone markers. Hedgerows of hawthorn bound the way, and beyond them fields of barley roll off in the breeze. The gatehouse lies behind you to the north, and the road carries on south between the hedges. The air smells of cut hay and wet earth.
rooms.105802: The road dips here to meet a rill that crosses it in a shallow ford, its bed paved with flat river stones so that cart wheels do not bog. Alder saplings lean over the water, and silt lies scattered across the gravel on the far side. Fields of turned earth stretch away to either hand, dark and ready for planting. The road runs back north the way you came and on south into the green country.
rooms.105803: Rooftops and chimney smoke show ahead where the road draws near the settlement, and the farmland gives way to kitchen gardens and low walls of piled stone. A leaning post bears an unlit tin lantern, and a hand-painted board beneath it points travellers on toward the town. The gravel is packed hard here by years of carts. North the road leads back toward the gatehouse, and south it enters the settlement.
rooms.105804: The gravel road widens into a muddy junction at the edge of the settlement, where a lane of beaten earth turns off east into Towne Road. Timber-framed cottages with steep thatched roofs crowd close, and a well with a mossy stone curb stands on the corner, its bucket chain rattling in the wind. Smoke curls from a dozen chimneys. The road runs on south between rail fences, and back north it leads toward the gatehouse.
rooms.105819: Towne Road is a lane of packed clay, rutted by cart wheels and edged with plank walkways raised above the mud. Cottage gables lean over it, window boxes crowded with marigolds and kale. Scrapings of boot-mud mark every doorstep, and a rusted horseshoe is nailed over one lintel for luck. The road runs east toward a wider crossing, and west it meets the gravel road.
rooms.105820: Four lanes meet at a crossing paved with round cobbles, the only paving for some distance. A gnawed hitching rail stands against one corner, and a notice board beside it hangs with bare pegs where papers once were pinned. Iron brackets on the corner walls hold lanterns for the evening. Towne Road leads north between cottages, east toward the heart of the town, south toward a school, and west back to the gravel road.
rooms.105821: The lane runs between two small cottages whose doors face each other across it, one painted green and the other a faded blue. Doorsteps are scrubbed white, and a boot scraper of bent iron waits beside each. A wash line sags across the lane, hung with linen that snaps in the wind. The east door opens on a cozy home and the west door on a quiet one, while the lane goes on north and back south to the crossing.
rooms.105822: Here the lane narrows between a house of squared logs and a plain cottage of whitewashed plaster. Rain barrels stand at their corners, and a woodpile stacked to the eaves fills the gap beside the log house. A cart wheel with a broken spoke leans on a fence as though forgotten. A door east leads into the log home and one west into the simple cottage, and the lane continues north to a dead end and south toward the crossing.
rooms.105823: The lane ends in a small circle of trampled earth ringed by three homes with their doors turned inward. A well-head of dry stone stands in the middle, capped with a wooden lid and roped shut against children. Faded chalk marks for some game cross the ground by the south mouth of the lane. Doors open north, east and west, and the lane leads back south to Towne Road.
rooms.105824: A single plain room serves this whole household, its plaster walls bare apart from a row of pegs for coats. A straw-tick bed sits in one corner under a patched quilt, and a table with two stools stands beneath the shuttered window. The hearth is swept clean and a blackened kettle hangs from its hook. The door south leads back out to the cul-de-sac.
rooms.105835: Bundles of reed show through the ceiling where the thatch has been laid thick over the rafters, giving the room a dry grassy smell. A spinning wheel waits beside the hearth with a hank of grey wool wound upon it, and herbs hang drying from the beams. The floor is beaten earth strewn with rushes. The door west opens back onto the cul-de-sac.
rooms.105834: This tiny cottage is scarcely wide enough for the narrow cot against the wall and the chest at its foot. A candle stub burns in a dish on the sill, and a rag rug covers the boards. A mended basket and a bundle of kindling hang from hooks beside the door. The door east opens onto the cul-de-sac.
rooms.105836: Round logs chinked with moss and clay make the walls of this snug home, and the smell of resin still lingers in the wood. A ladder-backed chair sits by an iron stove, and a shelf of crockery runs along the wall. A hunting bow hangs on two pegs above the door. The only way out is the door west, onto Towne Road.
rooms.105833: Plain furnishings fill this house: a trestle table, two benches and a dresser of blue-glazed plates. Sacking curtains hang across a sleeping alcove, and a broom leans in the corner near the cold hearth. Sunlight from a small window lays a bright square on the floor. The door east returns to Towne Road.
rooms.105837: A fire crackles in the hearth of this cozy home, and a deep armchair with a worn cushion sits beside it. Embroidered cloths cover the table and the mantel, and a pot of stew simmers on its hook above the coals. Dried flowers hang in bunches from the rafters. The door west opens on Towne Road.
rooms.105832: Hush lies on this house like a blanket, for the thick walls shut out the lane and the only sound is a clock ticking on its shelf. A rocking chair stands unmoving by a shuttered window with a folded shawl over its arm. Pale light filters through the slats onto a scrubbed floor. The door east gives onto Towne Road.
rooms.105838: The road here runs between shopfronts and workshops with their shutters thrown up for trade, and the packed clay is stained and pitted from hard use. A signboard creaks overhead on its chains, painted with a faded plough. Smells of baking drift along the lane from somewhere out of sight. The road leads east toward the square and west back to the crossing.
rooms.105882: Close to the square the road is cobbled at last, and the pavement rings under boots and cart wheels. Tall narrow houses with slate roofs lean in overhead, and a trough of carved stone stands against one wall, brimming from a brass spout. A bell tolls somewhere in the town, flat and slow. The square opens out east, and the road runs west the way you came.
rooms.105839: The square is a broad cobbled space with a stone fountain at its centre, its basin green with age and its spout dribbling a thin stream. Market stalls with sagging canvas awnings stand around the edge, waiting for the next market day. Towne Road leads away north and south, a park opens east beneath its trees, and the road west runs back toward the crossing. Whitewash and moss streak the fountain's rim.
rooms.105840: A short street of low shops, with the smell of frying onions pouring from the diner on the east side and a sharper, greener scent from the herbalist's door on the west. Bundles of dried lavender swing from a hook over the herbalist's step, and a chalkboard by the diner lists the day's dishes in tidy script. The road runs north into a smaller square and south to the great square.
rooms.105841: A small square paved with worn flagstones lies at the head of the street, with three doors opening off it: an apothecary's to the north, a clinic to the east and a smithy to the west. A pump with an iron handle stands in the middle, and the ring of hammer blows carries from the smithy. Soot streaks the walls on the west side. The street leads south toward the town square.
rooms.105842: Shelves of stoppered jars and glass bottles climb the walls of this narrow shop, each labelled in a tiny cramped hand. A counter scarred with acid stains holds brass scales and a mortar of dark stone, and the air is thick with camphor and clove. Dried roots hang in bunches near the ceiling. The way out is south, to the square.
rooms.105843: Clean linen and the sting of vinegar greet you in this whitewashed clinic. Narrow cots stand in a row beneath high windows, each made up with a grey blanket, and a table by the wall is laid with clamps, thread and bandages. A basin of steaming water sits by the door. West is the way out onto the square.
rooms.105844: The forge glows red at the back of this soot-black workshop, and a great bellows hangs wheezing beside it. An anvil scarred by years of hammering squats in the middle of the floor, ringed with tongs, punches and half-finished horseshoes. Heat shimmers over the quenching trough. A door east opens back onto the square.
rooms.105845: Salaylia's Diner is a warm low room of mismatched tables and benches worn smooth by elbows. A long counter runs along one wall, and behind it a hatch opens on a kitchen where pans clatter and something savoury bubbles. Tin lamps on the beams sway in the draught from the door. The only way out is west, to the road.
rooms.105846: Every beam and rafter of the herbalist's shop sags with drying bundles of leaf and flower, and the floor is cluttered with baskets of fresh-cut roots. A potted bay tree stands by the window, and a low table holds a ledger and a clay pot of ink. The smell is green and bitter and strangely soothing. The door east returns to the road.
rooms.105847: Flower beds blaze in reds, golds and violets across this little park, bordered with clipped box hedges and shaded by old maples. Gravel paths wind between benches carved with the names of long-dead sweethearts. A shady path leads north under arching boughs into the wood, the Towne Hall stands to the east, and the square lies back west. Fallen petals drift across the paths.
rooms.105848: The settlement's folk gather in this timbered hall to argue and settle accounts, and the high raftered ceiling swallows their voices. A long council table, scuffed and inkstained, runs the length of the floor, and a tattered banner of the baron's house hangs behind the reeve's chair. Benches line the walls beside a cabinet stuffed with rolled tax rolls. The door west leads out to the park.
rooms.105850: Towne Road passes here between a plain-fronted house of worship and a tailor's shop, where bolts of cloth hang in the window like banners. A scrap of faded ribbon is nailed beside the tailor's door as his sign, and a stone step worn hollow by many feet leads up to the worship house on the east side. The road leads north to the great square, south to a smaller one, and west through the tailor's door.
rooms.105851: A plain hall of whitewashed walls and dark beams, its benches set in rows before a low altar of grey stone. Candles in iron stands burn at either side, and light falls in coloured bars through one narrow window of stained glass. The air is cool and smells of wax and old incense. The door west opens to the road.
rooms.105853: A neat cobbled square, smaller than the great one, where carts pause to unload sacks and barrels. A rack of barrel staves stands against one wall, and the sour-sweet smell of mash hangs over everything from the distillery doorway east. A general store with a hanging lantern fills the west side, and a gated way south leads into gardens. The road leads back north toward the town square.
rooms.105854: Two squat copper stills dominate the Distillery, their coiled pipes dripping slowly into oaken tubs. Barrels in tall stacks line the walls, branded with the baron's mark, and the air is heavy and sweet enough to make the eyes water. A ladder leans against a mash vat crusted with grain. The only way out is the door west, onto the square.
rooms.105855: Walled beds of cabbages, beans and onions fill the Town Gardens in tidy rows, each plot marked by a stick with a scrap of coloured rag. A trellis hung with climbing peas shades a bench of weathered planks, and a rain butt stands at the corner of a toolshed. The soil is dark and freshly hoed, and the smell of crushed mint rises underfoot. A gap in the wall leads out north to the square.
rooms.105852: Shelves reach from floor to rafters in the General Store, crowded with rope, lamp oil, tin pans, nails and bolts of coarse cloth. A counter of scarred pine holds a ledger and a brass bell, and a barrel of pickled herring stands by the door. Boots, hats and sacks of meal hang from hooks overhead. The door east returns to the square.
rooms.105849: Bolts of wool, linen and dyed canvas lean against the walls of the tailor's shop, and a dressmaker's wooden form stands pinned in the middle of the floor. A long table carries shears, chalk and a tray of bone buttons, and a tape hangs from a nail beside the shuttered window. The floor is strewn with snippets of thread. A door in the east wall opens onto Towne Road.
rooms.105825: Towne Road runs south from the crossing between a freshly painted house on the east side and a boarded cottage on the west, whose door hangs half open. Whitewash drips have dried in streaks on the stones outside the painted house, and a ladder lies abandoned in its yard. Weeds grow between the cobbles in front of the empty one. The road leads north to the crossing and south to a small square.
rooms.105831: The smell of fresh paint fills this home, so sharp that the shutters have been propped wide. Everything is new and bright: a yellow-washed wall, a table scrubbed pale, and a bed with a quilt still creased from its folds. A pot of brushes soaks in a bucket by the hearth. The door west leads back to Towne Road.
rooms.105826: A small square of beaten earth lies before the schoolhouse, its ground scuffed bare by running feet. A hopscotch grid is scratched in one corner, and a bell on a bracket by the school door waits for its rope to be pulled. Two homes face each other across the open ground, one tidy to the east and one small to the west. The school stands south, and Towne Road leads back north.
rooms.105829: Everything in this home has a place and is in it: cups hang by their handles from a rack, boots stand in a neat pair by the door, and a rug has been brushed until its pattern shows. A tall clock stands in one corner, its pendulum swinging evenly. The hearth is blackleaded to a shine. The door west opens onto Schoolhouse Square.
rooms.105827: Rows of narrow desks with inkwells face a raised master's table in this old schoolroom, and a slate hangs on the wall still marked with half-erased sums. Letters of the alphabet are painted around the ceiling in faded red, and a cane rests on two hooks above the chalk-dusty blackboard. Sunlight slants through tall windows onto the boards. The door north leads out to the square.
rooms.105828: Barely more than a room with a bed, this small home is crowded with a loom that fills most of the floor. Half-woven cloth in blue and grey is stretched across it, and spools of thread sit in a basket by the stool. A pair of clogs waits beside the door. The door east leads back to Schoolhouse Square.
rooms.105830: No one has lived in this home for a long time, and dust lies thick on the table and the mantel. The shutters are nailed shut over the windows, and a few sticks of broken furniture are pushed against one wall. An old nest of dried mud clings above the lintel. Light enters only through the door east, which opens on Towne Road.
rooms.105805: The gravel road runs south past the last cottages, and open pasture rolls away on both sides behind walls of grey stacked stone. A stile of two worn steps crosses the wall at one point, and a milestone lettered with the baron's mark leans in the verge. Cart wheels have cut the gravel into twin troughs. The settlement lies back north, and the road goes on south.
rooms.105806: Willow and elder crowd a damp ditch at the roadside here, and the gravel is scattered with their small leaves. Posts of split oak march beside the road, strung with rusty wire, and a haystack under a thatched cap stands in a field. The wind brings a faint churning sound from far off, like a mill. The road runs north toward the settlement and south onward.
rooms.105807: The road turns here, bending off east around the corner of a ploughed field, and a crooked signpost marks the turning with arms bleached too pale to read. Furrows of rich brown soil run away in straight lines, and a scarecrow of sacking and sticks stands guard over them in a flapping coat. North the road returns toward the settlement, and east it bends on.
rooms.105808: A tall hedge of blackthorn walls the road on one side, thick with dark sloes, and a shallow ditch of brown water runs along its foot. The road swings here from the west and turns south toward a further bend. Pale dust lifts from the gravel at each footfall and settles slowly again.
rooms.105809: A lone ash tree stands at the elbow of this bend in the gravel road, and its roots have heaved the verge into a low mound. Carters have worn a pale path around its trunk where they swing their wagons wide. The road comes down from the north and curves away east, and the smell of hay and manure drifts along it from further on.
rooms.105810: The road curves again, swinging in from the west to run south toward a large barn whose red roof shows above a stand of poplars. Puddles fill the ruts, and the gravel is darkened with old straw dragged out by wheels. A fence of whitewashed rails begins here and follows the road. The air is thick with the scent of dung and hay.
rooms.105811: A large barn of weathered red boards towers over a yard of trampled earth, its double doors slid back on rusted tracks. Straw and spilled grain mark the ground, and a water trough hollowed from a single log stands by the wall. The road leads north back to the bend, and a lane runs east to the baron's tower, whose dark bulk looms above the roofline. The barn's open doors face south.
rooms.105812: A track of packed earth runs on toward the baron's tower, its bulk rising dark and unlovely over the roofs of sheds and byres. The grass along the verge has been cut short and the hedges clipped hard, as though some stern eye insisted on it. A rusty lantern pole stands here without a lantern. The track runs east toward the tower and west back to the barn yard.
rooms.105813: The lane widens into a bare yard of swept flagstones, and the keep rises sheer above it, black-grey stone studded with narrow slit windows. The ivy clinging to the walls has died to a brittle brown, and no bird sings here. A cold breath seems to come off the masonry. The gate lies east, and west the lane leads back toward the barn.
rooms.105814: An arched gateway of iron-bound oak stands in the tower's base, and over it the baron's arms are cut deep in the stone: a tower between two crescents. Twin braziers burn low on either side of the door, and the flagstones before it are worn to hollows by countless feet. The great door east stands ajar on a dark entry, and the lane leads back west.
rooms.105856: A cold, narrow entry hall with a floor of black flags and a vaulted ceiling hung with iron lanterns. Coat pegs line one wall, though no coats hang there, and the rushes underfoot smell of tallow and damp. A pair of tall doors carved with thorns stands open east into a larger hall, and the door west returns to the gate.
rooms.105857: The main hall is a long lofty chamber, its grey pillars hung with banners of the barony gone brown with soot. A wide hearth on one side holds a fire that gives more smoke than warmth, and high windows throw dim bars of daylight across the floor. A doorway north leads to a feasting hall, an arch east opens on an audience chamber, and the entryway lies west.
rooms.105861: A long table of black oak runs down the middle of this hall, set with pewter plates and cold candlesticks laid for guests who never came. Antler racks and hunting horns hang from the walls, and the great hearth is swept clean and empty. Dust lies on the benches, undisturbed. The hall goes on east, and a doorway south leads back to the main hall.
rooms.105860: The far end of the feasting hall is raised on a shallow dais, where a high seat carved with wolves faces down the length of the table. Tall shuttered windows frame the dais, and a stale smell of old wine hangs in the heavy curtains. Broken goblets are swept into a corner. A door south opens on the audience chamber, and the hall stretches back west.
rooms.105858: A grand chamber of tall windows, with a dais at the far end whose steps are carpeted in crimson worn to the thread. The Gilded Chair stands upon it, its gold leaf peeling, facing a floor of chequered marble. Doors lead north to the feasting hall and south to a private meeting room, an arch opens west to the main hall, and a narrow door east lies behind the dais.
rooms.105859: A narrow space is hidden behind the dais, curtained from the chamber by heavy velvet that smells of age. The back of the Gilded Chair looms overhead, bare wood without any gilding, and cobwebs hang in the corners. A gap in the panelling reveals a tight stair rising up into darkness. The door west leads back to the audience chamber.
rooms.105863: A narrow spiral of worn steps winds through the thickness of the tower wall, so tight that the shoulders brush mortar on both sides. A single torch gutters in an iron ring, and its smoke blackens the low ceiling. Scratch marks of countless hands have polished the rail. The stair leads up toward the upper floors and down to the space behind the gilded chair.
rooms.105864: Rough mortar and unpolished stone line this hallway, and the chill here is a different cold from the damp of the lower rooms. Wall sconces hold black candles, and their flames lean toward the doors. A heavy door south bears a sign of crossed bones, and the hall continues west. A stair leads down to the secret spiral.
rooms.105870: Black drapes cover the windows of these chambers, and a ring of pale candles burns upon a table scattered with charts and bone-handled knives. Shelves line the walls, crowded with skulls arranged by size, and a sweet, faint rot underlies the incense. A great open book lies on a reading stand. The door north returns to the hallway, and an inner room lies west.
rooms.105869: The inner room is small and cold, with a narrow cot made up in grey sheets and a cabinet of tinctures standing open. A mirror on the wall has been turned face to the plaster, and a bowl of black water sits untouched on the sill. Something has been scratched into the floorboards in a circle. The only way out is east, to the outer chambers.
rooms.105865: The hallway bends here, and the air carries a sharp odour of sulphur from the door to the north. Black stains streak the mortar around its frame, and the floor before it is scorched in a pale circle. Torches burn in brackets, smoking. The hall runs east to the stairhead and west to its end.
rooms.105867: Glass tubes, brass funnels and bell jars crowd the benches of this chamber, and a rack of stoppered phials glints in the light of a green-shaded lamp. The floor is scrubbed in patches, as though something spilled there and was hastily wiped away. Charts of the human frame, inked in red, are pinned to every wall. The door south opens on the hallway, and an archway leads west to a back room.
rooms.105868: This back room holds a high narrow table with leather straps hanging from its sides, and a trough beneath it drains through a slot in the floor. Shelves of jars hold pale shapes floating in murky spirits, and the smell of vinegar and iron lies thick on the air. A stool and a tray of surgeon's saws wait beside the table. Nothing else leads from the room but the archway east.
rooms.105866: The hall ends in a blank wall hung with a faded tapestry of a stag hunt, its colours dulled by smoke. A narrow bench stands beneath it, and a cracked bowl of dried petals perfumes the corner with a lost summer. Drafts rattle a loose shutter somewhere overhead. A hall runs back east, and a door west leads into a sitting room.
rooms.105871: This sitting room is warm and well kept, with two deep chairs drawn up before a hearth and a rug of dark red wool between them. A carved cabinet of decanters stands against the wall, and a lamp with a painted shade casts a gentle gold glow. Doors open north to a bathing area and south to private chambers, and a hall lies back east. A stair of runed stone climbs up from the corner.
rooms.105874: A deep copper tub stands on clawed feet in the middle of the bathing area, a folded towel draped over its rim. Steam from a kettle of hot water clouds the mirror above a washstand, and sweet-smelling soaps lie in a dish of blue glass. The floor tiles are warm underfoot, and a rack holds fresh linen. The only way out is south, to the sitting room.
rooms.105872: The baron's private chambers open here with a great four-post bed hung with curtains of dark green velvet. A writing desk stands by the window, its surface strewn with letters sealed in black wax and a seal-ring pressed in a dish. A tall mirror in a gilt frame reflects the room, a little dimmer than the room itself. A door leads north to the sitting room, and the chambers extend east.
rooms.105873: A wardrobe of black oak, a trunk bound with brass and a rack of heavy cloaks fill the inner part of the baron's chambers. A carved panel beside the wardrobe stands slightly out of true, and a draught rises from behind it with the smell of cold air. The floor around it is worn to a bright path. The chambers continue back west, and a hidden stair leads down behind the panel.
rooms.105883: A hidden stair drops steeply from the baron's chambers, its steps cut narrow and slick with a sheen of damp. The walls are bare grey masonry, and a hand rope of knotted hemp is the only rail. Faint hollow sounds rise from below, a murmur that might be chanting. The stair leads up to the chambers above and down into deeper darkness.
rooms.105884: The stair ends in a small landing, where the steps turn and the air grows heavier and colder. An iron ring is set in the wall, holding a torch that burns with a pale, steady flame and no smoke. The masonry is damp, and dull marks have been scraped across it as if by nails. A passage leads north, and the steps climb up the way you came.
rooms.105885: The passage is low and bare, its walls lined with small niches that hold stubs of candles burned down to wax. Ahead the light changes, going dim and violet, as if the day were forever fading. Every footstep sounds muffled and strangely close. The passage opens north into a great chamber, and a landing lies south.
rooms.105886: You stand at the edge of a vast chamber lit by a dim violet glow that has no source. The floor is black polished glass, and your reflection walks beneath your feet. Tall pillars of grey stone rise into a ceiling lost in haze, and the air hums low. A passage returns south, and the chamber stretches away north, east and west.
rooms.105891: The heart of the chamber is a wide circle of black glass inlaid with silver lines, curved and branching like roots. Violet light pools here and flickers as though at the bottom of deep water. The hum swells to a thrum you feel in the teeth. The glass floor continues in every direction, north, east, south and west.
rooms.105893: A tall curtain of grey gauze hangs along the far wall, stirring in a wind that does not blow anywhere else in the chamber. Behind it, shadows seem to shift and gather, taller than any man. The glass floor is cold even through boots. The chamber continues east and west along the wall, and opens back south toward its centre.
rooms.105894: The corner of the chamber is crowded with shattered glass, swept into heaps against the walls, and the pillars here are cracked from base to capital. Silver lines in the floor end at a ragged hole, filled in with black wax. The violet light is faintest in this place. The chamber lies back south and west.
rooms.105890: A line of iron braziers stands cold along the wall, each filled with white ash that stirs when you pass. The violet haze thickens near the ceiling, making the pillars look unfinished. Silver lines in the floor bend toward a pillar at the edge of the room. The chamber extends north and south from here, and opens back west toward its centre.
rooms.105889: Chalk marks cover the glass floor in a rough arc here, symbols and numbers overwritten again and again until they are a grey smear. A stool and a stand of rolled parchments stand at the edge of the arc, long untouched. The haze is thin, and the air tastes of old coins. The chamber stretches north and west from this corner.
rooms.105892: A wall of mirrors in black frames lines this corner, though every glass has been cracked or turned to the plaster, and a single one shows a different room entirely. The pillars close in, leaving a narrow way between them. The hum is quieter here, almost soothing. The chamber opens east toward its far side and south along the wall.
rooms.105888: Long black drapes hang from the pillars here, rippling in the thrumming air, and in their folds the violet light turns to indigo. A carved stone bench faces the wall, its seat worn smooth by long vigils. Tracks of dust show where something heavy was dragged across the floor. The chamber extends north and south, and opens east toward its centre.
rooms.105887: The edge of the chamber is quiet and dim, and the glass underfoot shows only a pale blur of your own face. A tall rack of silver rods leans against the wall, each tipped with a crystal that gives off a dull violet gleam. The air smells faintly of burnt hair. The chamber extends north and east from here.
rooms.105875: A narrow stair of black stone spirals up from the sitting room, its steps cut with runes that glow faintly as you pass. The walls are smooth and cold, and a thin humming comes from above. Candle-smoke has stained the ceiling in a soft grey. The stair climbs up toward the laboratory and descends back to the sitting room.
rooms.105876: The laboratory fills a round chamber under the tower roof, and benches ring its walls beneath hanging copper lamps. Retorts, alembics and long glass coils crowd every surface, and some still bubble over beds of blue flame. A scorched floor shows where past experiments went badly. The laboratory continues east, a study opens south, and a runed stair descends.
rooms.105877: A great iron furnace squats at the heart of the lab, its mouth glowing orange and its flue vanishing into the roof. Tongs, bellows and ladles hang from a rail, and the floor is gritty with soot swept to one side. The heat is fierce, and the air shimmers. The laboratory runs back west, and a low door in the south wall leads to an artifact room.
rooms.105881: Glass cases line the walls of this small room, their locks of black iron, each holding some strange relic: a skull inlaid with silver, a tarnished crown, an iron hand. Dust has been wiped from the glass in neat circles, as though the cases are opened often. A heavy brass balance stands on a pedestal in the middle. The only way out is north, to the laboratory.
rooms.105878: Candles by the dozen burn in iron holders around this study, and the wax has run in long white drips on every desk. A great table is covered with open books and unfinished letters, and a skull holds down a pile of parchments. The smell of ink and tallow is strong. The study opens north to the laboratory and south to a library.
rooms.105879: Shelves rise to the ceiling in this packed library, bowed by the weight of leather-bound books and rolled scrolls. A ladder on a rail runs the length of the wall, and the aisles between the stacks are scarcely wide enough for one reader. Dust motes drift in the light of a single window. The study lies back north, and a short passage leads east to an observatory.
rooms.105880: The observatory is a small round room under a dome of dark timber, with a slot cut in its roof for a long brass tube set on a swivelling mount. Star charts cover the walls, marked with crimson lines that converge on one point. A stool and an inkwell wait beneath the instrument. The only way out is west, to the library.
rooms.105862: A small round table with four chairs stands in this meeting room, its surface scarred by the knives and rings of long discussions. A tall cabinet of ledgers stands against the wall, and a single narrow window admits a pale slice of light. The walls are panelled in dark wood, and a stale smell of pipe-smoke lingers. The only way out is north, to the audience chamber.
rooms.105815: The Scrupulously Clean Barn has a floor swept bare and stalls scrubbed with lye until the boards are nearly white. Tools hang in neat order on pegs, and bales of hay are stacked square against the walls. Light falls in long gold bars through slits in the planking and shows not a mote of dust. The barn doors open north to the yard, and an inner door leads south to the pastures.
rooms.105816: A wide meadow opens here behind the barn, the grass cropped short and bright green, with a stout rail fence marking its edges. A trough of rainwater stands by the barn wall, ringed with trampled mud. The sky is large and the breeze smells of clover. The barn door lies north, and the pasture continues east and west.
rooms.105817: The pasture rises to a low mound here where a pair of old oaks cast broad shade, and the grass beneath them is flattened in rings. A rotting gate lies in the long grass, half-sunk. Buttercups dot the slope and the air hums with insects. The pasture slopes back west toward the barn.
rooms.105818: This end of the pasture is boggy and ill-drained, a place of rushes and trampled mud where the grass gives way to dark puddles. A fence of leaning rails marks the edge of the baron's land, and a battered bucket lies on its side. The wind moves the rushes in long whispers. The pasture lies back east toward the barn.

creatures.long_desc: A weary farmhand leans on a pitchfork, staring blankly at the ground.
creatures.description: A sunburnt man in a patched smock, his hands cracked and his eyes shadowed with sleeplessness. He glances often toward the tower and says little.

creatures.long_desc: A wary villager hurries along, eyes down and shoulders tight.
creatures.description: A plain, homespun-clad townsperson of the settlement, who carries a basket and speaks little to strangers. They keep their voices low and glance often at the dark tower.

creatures.long_desc: A grim tower guard stands watch, halberd planted and eyes hard.
creatures.description: A broad guard in a black-and-grey livery with the baron's tower on the breast. His helm hides most of his face, and his halberd is notched with use.

creatures.long_desc: A robed cultist mutters over a book, black sleeves smeared with ash.
creatures.description: A pale figure in a dark hooded robe stitched with silver thread, his fingers stained with ink and something darker. His eyes are fixed and unblinking.

creatures.long_desc: A dusk-pale ghost drifts across the glass, trailing violet mist.
creatures.description: A tall, translucent shape in the tatters of a robe, bound to the chamber by whatever work the baron began. Its hollow eyes burn with faint violet light.

creatures.long_desc: A stitched ogre hulks over the benches, seams of thread crossing its grey hide.
creatures.description: A towering brute sewn together from parts that were never meant to match, one arm longer than the other. Black thread binds every seam, and a dull glow lights its eyes.

creatures.long_desc: Gilzaan, the baron's adviser, bends over a table of knives and glass, whispering to himself.
creatures.description: A gaunt, bald man in a stained leather apron, his fingers long and stained with chemicals. He looks up with the mild interest of a man spared from boredom.

creatures.short_desc: Baron Kalveh, lord of the fief
creatures.long_desc: Baron Kalveh stands in the violet gloom, his hands wreathed in pale fire.
creatures.description: A tall, grey-haired lord in a black cloak clasped with a silver tower, his face as handsome as a statue and as cold. The light of the chamber bends toward him as he moves.

items.description: A long-hafted halberd with a black-grey blade, nicked from hard use. The baron's tower is stamped into its socket.

items.room_desc: A hooded black robe lies crumpled here.
items.description: A heavy robe of black wool stitched with silver thread in a pattern of crescents. It smells faintly of ash and old ink.

items.room_desc: A shimmering violet shroud lies here.
items.description: A thin cloak woven of something that is not quite cloth, it deepens to indigo at the hem. It never seems to settle and moves like mist on the air.

items.room_desc: A stained ironwood staff lies here.
items.description: A heavy staff of dark ironwood capped with a ball of tarnished brass. Chemical stains discolour its lower end.

items.room_desc: A long black blade lies here, cold to the eye.
items.description: A long sword of dark metal with a pommel shaped like a tower, whose edge seems to drink the light. It is the finest weapon the fief has known, and it has seen terrible use.
